scope.q: What is the current average time doctors spend on notes outside of patient contact hours, and what is the target reduction?
scope.why: Quantifying the problem helps set clear success metrics and prioritize features that deliver the most impact on time savings.

scope.q: What specific types of patient encounters and corresponding note templates are the primary focus for automation?
scope.why: Understanding the variability in note types and structures is crucial for determining the feasibility and complexity of automated generation.

scope.q: How do doctors currently review and approve notes, and what are the non-negotiable legal or compliance requirements for note finalization?
scope.why: Defining the approval workflow and regulatory constraints early will ensure the solution integrates seamlessly and meets all necessary standards.

decomposition.title: Audio Capture & Transcription
decomposition.why: Accurate conversion of spoken interactions to text is foundational for all subsequent AI processing.

decomposition.title: Clinical Information Extraction
decomposition.why: Identifying and structuring key medical entities and concepts from raw transcripts is essential for generating coherent notes.

decomposition.title: Note Generation & Templating
decomposition.why: Automating the drafting of notes into specific, pre-defined clinical templates saves significant manual effort.

decomposition.title: Clinician Review & Edit UI
decomposition.why: Providing an intuitive interface for doctors to efficiently review, edit, and approve notes ensures clinical accuracy and buy-in.

decomposition.title: EHR Integration & Sync
decomposition.why: Seamlessly pushing approved notes into the existing Electronic Health Record system is critical for operational workflow.

sprint.title: Audio Capture & Basic Transcription Setup
sprint.deliv: Working endpoint for audio upload, returns raw text transcript of a 5-minute test audio file.

sprint.title: Clinical Entity Extraction PoC
sprint.deliv: Demonstration extracting patient name, chief complaint, and key medications from a sample transcript.

sprint.title: Single Template Note Generation
sprint.deliv: System generates a draft note for a specific encounter type (e.g., follow-up) based on extracted entities.

sprint.title: Review UI & Basic Editing
sprint.deliv: Web interface displays a generated draft note, allowing a doctor to view and make text edits.

sprint.title: EHR Integration (Read-Only) & Approval Workflow
sprint.deliv: Approved notes can be marked as 'final' in the system, and basic patient context can be pulled from EHR.

sprint.title: End-to-End Workflow Demo
sprint.deliv: Full cycle: audio capture to approved note displayed in the review UI, ready for EHR submission.

risks.risk: Transcription accuracy in noisy clinical environments or with varied accents may be poor.
risks.mitigation: Implement robust noise reduction algorithms and evaluate multiple transcription models, potentially fine-tuning with clinic-specific audio data.

risks.risk: AI-generated notes might contain factual errors or omissions, leading to patient safety issues or legal liability.
risks.mitigation: Design a mandatory, explicit clinician review and approval step for every note, clearly marking AI-generated content for scrutiny. Start with low-risk note types.

risks.risk: Integration with the existing EHR system proves more complex or restrictive than anticipated.
risks.mitigation: Begin with a read-only integration for patient context, then develop a phased write-back strategy in close collaboration with the EHR vendor or IT team, focusing on their APIs and data standards.

risks.risk: Clinicians may resist adopting new workflows or distrust AI-generated content, leading to low usage.
risks.mitigation: Involve clinicians early in design, provide comprehensive training, and highlight demonstrable time savings. Ensure the review UI is intuitive and faster than manual note-taking.
